transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-14
Time: 15:00 - 16:02 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Ramirez (Redwood AE); Ethan Cole (Redwood SE); Daniel Price (Cobalt Procurement); Maya Lin (Cobalt Legal); Arjun Patel (Cobalt CTO); Lena Cho (Cobalt Head of ML Infra)
Links shared: https://redwood.com/security-whitepaper (noted), pricing sheet (redacted link), draft MSA (customer provided)

Summary:
Quick intake between Redwood AE/SE and Cobalt procurement + legal to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA expectations, pricing approval path and pilot scope. High interest in private VPC deployment with KMS integration; procurement wants clear egress and data residency clauses and a staging-to-prod ramp for pricing.

Topics discussed:
- MSA redlines around indemnity and data residency
- DPA requirements for EU vs US data
- SLA percentage and remedies (credits vs termination)
- Pricing models: committed reserved capacity vs pay-as-you-go
- KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML, SOC2 reporting
- Pilot scope, benchmarks, and technical preflight

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time today. we have about an hour, is that right?
00:06 Daniel (Cobalt): yes 60 minutes works. morning/afternoon all. i'm daniel, procurement lead.
00:12 Sofia: great. quick intros? ethan from our solutions engineering team will help with technicals.
00:18 Ethan (Redwood): hey hi all, ethan cole here, se working on onboarding and perf testing for infra teams.
00:24 Maya (Cobalt): maya lin, i'm counsel for cobalt. i'll focus on the dpa/msa language and security obligations.
00:30 Arjun (Cobalt): arjun patel, cto. will speak to infra, data residency and latency needs.
00:34 Lena (Cobalt): lena cho, head of ml infra, will own pilot and benchmarks.
00:39 Sofia: perfect. So agenda — i want to align on your procurement timeline, any non-negotiable contract items, and the pilot scope that will unlock pricing. then we can agree next steps.
00:48 Daniel: timeline: procurement committee meets 2/25, legal signoff ideally by 3/5. we need pricing committed by 2/20 to hit finance windows.
00:57 Maya: i'll likely push back on indemnity and deletion clauses. also want to confirm SOC 2 type ii and audit logs retention — we need at least 12 months of immutable audit trails.
01:05 Ethan: noted. we provide SOC2 type 2 attestation; audit logs are exportable to customer S3; retention windows can be configured. one caveat is for hosted tier logs are managed by our control plane but can be forwarded.
01:16 Arjun: for latency and compliance reasons we prefer private deployment in our VPC — can you confirm private option for redwood private and whether KMS/HSM integration is supported?
01:25 Sofia: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC deployment and customer-managed KMS. there are on-prem options too if needed, but i want to be clear on the SLA and cost delta — private has a higher baseline and setup fees.
01:38 Daniel: procurement will need a clear breakdown: one-time setup, monthly committed capacity cost, and egress fees. any hidden costs around model updates?
01:47 Sofia: good question. model upgrades are included in our service for hosted and dedicated; for private we have optional managed upgrades or customer-managed paths — we'll include upgrade options in the pricing sheet.
01:58 Maya: on the msa redlines, the indemnity cap in the draft seems low. we also need data residency clauses: our eu customer PII must remain in EU regions and any backups must follow the same.
02:07 Ethan: we support region pinning per workload. we do automated routing to ensure requests for EU tenants stay in EU capacity pools. small transcription note: sometimes the log name shows as K V cache in the transcript — it's K-V cache.
02:20 Lena: for the pilot we'd like a canary that mirrors our prod traffic shape: 800 token average, peak p90 latency under 150ms for standard gen. can you commit to that in a pilot SLA?
02:31 Ethan: pilot slas are configurable. we can run a perf run and provide a benchmark report. production SLA numbers would be per contract — 99.9 for hosted, higher for dedicated. we can propose 99.95 for dedicated pools.
02:45 Arjun: what's the remediation for missed slas? are there credits, or termination rights after sustained failures?
02:51 Sofia: standard approach is service credits; larger enterprise deals can negotiate termination triggers for chronic failures. legal will need to align on thresholds — often it's x days of outage within a window.
03:03 Maya: we want to avoid lengthy credit-only remedies; some of our board requires termination or change in service if critical breaches happen. also need clarity on data deletion — if we terminate, can we attest that customer data and logs are purged within 30 days and KMS keys destroyed?
03:18 Ethan: for private we can do customer-managed keys; destruction policy depends on the key provider. we can provide a certificate of deletion for logs and data snapshots; for hosted we have documented retention and deletion process.
03:30 Daniel: pricing: if we commit to 6 months reserved capacity what's the discount and can we start with a small reserved baseline and burst to shared capacity?
03:39 Sofia: yes, committed baseline plus burst model is typical. discounts scale with commitment. i'll send two pricing scenarios: 6-month and 12-month commitments and the incremental burst rates.
03:48 Lena: also need telemetry details: token-level cost, latency by route, and per-model cost breakdown for our FinTeam to justify spend.
03:56 Ethan: the console exposes per-token breakdown, model-level dashboards, traces, and you can also forward raw usage logs to your S3 for finops. small caveat: sample rates for high throughput to avoid huge volumes but we'll provide the raw export for pilot.
04:10 Maya: on security, can you confirm SOC2 cert date and a redacted scope? also do you support SSO via SAML and SCIM for user provisioning?
04:19 Sofia: SOC2 report is current — we'll share a redacted attestation. we support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, RBAC with granular roles and audit trails.
04:28 Arjun: are there any export controls or embargoed country limitations we need to be aware of for crypto models or certain data types?
04:35 Ethan: we do comply with export control lists; certain model features may be restricted by region — we'll include that in the security pack.
04:42 Daniel: procurement wants a single commercial point-of-contact and a contract lifecycle spreadsheet so approvals can be tracked — can you provide that?
04:49 Sofia: yes, i'll provide a contract tracker template and the pricing workbook. I'll also include a short note on redlines we've already accepted.
04:58 Maya: i will send the MSA redlines. expect standard exceptions around indemnity and possibly a carve-out for regulatory subpoenas.
05:06 Ethan: technical note — for the pilot we'll need a connectivity checklist: firewall rules, VPC peering or private link, KMS ARN, and example workload to simulate. i'll draft that.
05:20 Lena: timeline check: we need pilot started by 2/24 to collect 7 days of telemetry before procurement committee. is that workable?
05:28 Sofia: tight but doable. if we get the signed SOW by 2/18 and keys/config by 2/21 we can spin up a pilot env by 2/23.
05:38 Daniel: procurement approval on 2/25 still our target. legal signoff by 3/5 per earlier.
05:45 Maya: noted. one more on liability: do you carry cyber insurance? limits?
05:50 Sofia: yes we have cyber liability insurance; i'll share the cert and limits in the pack.
05:56 Ethan: i'll also include a suggested benchmark harness — we frequently instrument microbursts and long-seq tests because cost and kernel selection vary with sequence length.
06:06 Arjun: do you support quantized models to reduce cost? we may want quantized fp8 variants for lower-cost inference.
06:14 Ethan: yes we have quantized variants and recommendations in the optimize pack; they affect latency tradeoffs and quality. we'll include example quality regressions we'd expect.
06:25 Maya: okay that's helpful. i'll try to consolidate redlines and aim to get them to you by 2/21.
06:32 Sofia: recap — sofia to send pricing scenarios, redwood security pack, soc2 attestation and contract tracker by 2/18; ethan to send pilot connectivity checklist and benchmark template by 2/20; customer will send MSA redlines by 2/21. pilot target start 2/23, procurement decision 2/25.
06:46 Daniel: sounds good. thanks all.
06:48 Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email. link to shared drive will include the pricing and pilot plan.

End of transcript
